mainEntity.name: Is a dedicated team really dedicated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dedicated means assigned to your accounts under the scope we write down. We describe exactly who works on what.

mainEntity.name: Can your team speak to my clients?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if you invite them as part of your team. Otherwise they stay behind the scenes.

mainEntity.name: Which time zones do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: We agree overlap hours with you during onboarding.

mainEntity.name: What tools can the team use?
Will my client know MMC is involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you choose to tell them. We sign an NDA, work under your brand, send deliverables in your format and do not contact your clients unless you ask us to.

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell us the roles you need and your tools. After the NDA we propose a team and an onboarding plan.

answer.label: In short
answer.lead: Agency outsourcing means handing delivery work to a partner so your team can focus on clients and sales. With MMC you can hire a dedicated team, or draw hours as needed, of strategists, designers, developers and writers who work inside your processes, under your brand and an NDA.

stages.why: Salaries run before the projects arrive, and your margin carries the gap.
stages.does: We scope a pod to the work you have, and seats can be added or paused as the pipeline changes.

stages.breaks: Losing the person who knew the account.
stages.why: Each handover to a new freelancer costs weeks of context and a drop in quality.
stages.does: A named pod stays on your accounts, with a second person briefed on each, so one absence does not stall the work.

stages.why: Chat threads lose decisions, and no one is sure which version is final.
stages.does: Briefs, drafts and approvals live on one board with an owner for each item.

stages.breaks: Letting the partner use their own tools.
stages.why: You lose sight of progress, and moving a project back in-house becomes a rescue job.
stages.does: The pod works in your tracker, drive and templates, under your processes, so you always see the work.

stages.breaks: Checking quality only when something breaks.
stages.why: Small slips accumulate when no one is looking, and your client notices before you do.
stages.does: A weekly review with you, a checklist per deliverable and a coordinator who tracks the open items.
